main_text.p: confensus zeleafe, & leafniȷ, unde nostrum, eodem sensu, leatbe, i.e. licentia, quod Belg. Dozlof, bet-lof. Germ. Erlaab, Erlaubnus.
Bellboze, Libera] Hoc, ut & nostrum dellber, latinizant.
Delibedelit, Deprecabilis] Saxon. biodan, est orare, rogare, precari, cujus (ni fallor) in hac voce quale quale vestigium.
Gemerka, Terminus] Finis, terminus Sax. zemaṗne. unde hodie agrorum fines sive limites metres, alias meers, vocamus. Mark alias meart, & mareb, eodem sensu utimur.
Gibert, Libera. vide gebere] Hoc Sax. zeṗṗéo, ab eorum zeṗṗean, Belg. brpen, Teut. frejen, liberare, quo sensu nostrum to free, vel set free.

Genubte, Abundantia: ab eo quod nos genoech, satis. vide genubtegot. Genubt samozt, Uberi] Copia, abundantia, Sax. zeniþtrumnyrye ? Satis autem zenoþ, unde nostrum enough. Hinc uber (adject.) Sax. zeniþtrum i casu ablat. zenithtrumpe ?

page.notes: Gothic (black letter) words are rendered as best read; the bottom lines are cut off at the page edge and the catchword is uncertain. Several Old Saxon forms are doubtful and marked only by their letters as read.
